findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If receivedData contains a format string like '%s' or '%n'
findings.assumptions: The code does not show any indication of command execution, but the use of printf with untrusted input is suspicious and could lead to format string vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: If the received data is larger than sizeof(uint32_t)
findings.assumptions: The code assumes that recvfrom will not receive more data than sizeof(uint32_t), but this is not enforced.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: If receivedData is the maximum uint32_t value
findings.assumptions: The code does not handle the case where receivedData could be the maximum uint32_t value, which could lead to unexpected behavior.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If receivedData contains special characters or sequences that could alter the behavior of the printf function
findings.assumptions: The code does not neutralize special characters in receivedData before using it in printf.
